title: Integral scalar extension preserves bounded constructible integral complexes
statement: Let $E\subset L$ be finite extensions of $\Ql$ with valuation rings $\mathcal O_E\subset\mathcal O_L$, with $\ell\neq p$, and let $Y$ be a scheme. For every $K\in D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], the integral scalar extension $K\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L$ [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension] lies in $D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_L)$. Hence integral scalar extension restricts to an $\mathcal O_E$-linear functor $D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)\to D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_L)$.

source.place: last paragraph (the functor $-\otimes_EL:D^b_c(Y,E)\to D^b_c(Y,L)$ is defined on integral representatives, which presupposes this); also asserted in dag node lem-coef-integral-finite-extension ('This exact functor preserves the integral bounded constructible categories')

proof.text: J4 legacy reduction: choose a complex representative of K by essential surjectivity of DerivedCategory.Q, then its K-flat resolution with flat terms. The tensor-right comparison transports termwise exactness to the recorded IsFlatOnSite property, giving a good representative and a derived isomorphism to K. Its bounded constructible property transfers by isomorphism closure. Extract the common interval and the source residue reduction. Apply lem-sf-integral-scalar-finite-level-bounds to obtain target finite tensor constructibility and bounds; apply lem-sf-integral-scalar-tower-effectivity for completeness and isomorphisms from the actual target reductions to these finite complexes. Transfer the finite properties through those isomorphisms, then transfer the assembled integral property along scalar extension of the representative isomorphism. Restricted linearity follows directly from the ambient coefficient action and the unique canonical Linear formulas. The ordinary constructibility and final restricted-comparison holes are retained; retain the previously proved completion-chain and restricted-linearity arguments. A private component equation for the ordinary scalar model and controlled transparency avoid expanding sheafification data during the tensor transport; the zero-coordinate rewrite uses the preadditive composition-with-zero identity.

The ambient integral scalar-extension functor is $R$-linear by clause 3 of [lem-weil-integral-scalar-extension-well-defined]. Step 7 shows that it sends every object of the integral bounded constructible full subcategory into the corresponding full subcategory for $S$. Restrict its object and morphism maps to these full subcategories. The equality $T(af)=aT(f)$ on ambient morphisms is the same equality on their full-subcategory Hom groups. This is the asserted $R$-linear functor.

proof.text: For the intrinsic Lean interface, identify IsSfDerivedComplete with the legacy K-flat augmented-tower predicate using lem-sf-derived-complete-legacy-comparison. The finite reduction functors are definitionally identical and the common support interval is the same condition. Choose a prime q greater than l and the datum with base field ULift(ZMod q); no structure on Y is introduced. Apply the already published legacy integralScalarExtension_constructible, which carries the preceding mathematical proof plan, then transfer the result back to sfIntegralConstructible. The existing ambient linearity proof restricts unchanged. This compatibility proof relies on the existing legacy preservation sorry; it does not independently prove the preceding finite-filtration argument.

For the legacy completion-chain interface, identify integralCompletedScalarMap with completedCoefficientMap by their finite projection uniqueness. The two ordinary scalar functors have the same sheafified tensor objects and maps, yielding a natural isomorphism whose components are the specified equality transports. Precompose completedScalarChainComparison with this isomorphism on complexes. Its tensor formula gives the prescribed quotient coordinate; its shifted coordinate remains zero. To show uniqueness, tensor generation makes the quotient coordinates equal, product projections give equality of the first cocone coordinate, and the zero shifted coordinates give equality of the second. The biproduct identity for the mapping cocone gives degreewise equality, hence equality of natural transformations. This closes only integralScalarCompletionChain_existsUnique; preservation of constructibility and the final restricted derived comparison remain unproved. The restricted-linearity declaration is proved separately by the ambient coefficient-action equality and the inherited full-subcategory Hom action.
